dimensions.note: No secrets in settings; the Jev key lives in the separate @swamp/typesafe-ai instance, from a vault. A task whose text looks like a token, key, password or email is withheld and never sent. The heading now sent with each task is checked the same way and left out of the question when it looks like a secret (tested, and checked end to end against a mock Jev that logged every question).

run logs task, withheld, question and batch counts; classify logs task and answer counts, summed across batches (tested with two batches). Task text, headings and note paths are never logged (tested).

Folder containment and existence are checked before any note is read, and only NotFound is caught. batchSize must be a whole number of at least 1 (tested). A failed Jev request fails only its own forEach step (allowFailure), and classify runs whatever the ask job's outcome.

34 tests on temp vaults, no network, including headings, batching, the batchSize setting, three-way answers, answers merged across batches, the upgrade entry and secret-looking headings. The workflow was also run end to end against a mock Jev: all batches answered, every second batch failing, Jev unreachable; templates and daily notes left out, withheld tasks never sent, vault checksum unchanged.

The vault is only read (tested; end-to-end checksum unchanged). A failed batch leaves its tasks unclassified and the next run asks again. The ask job reads the batches with data.latest because forEach.in resolves at job start; if two runs overlapped, answers for task ids the run did not list are ignored by classify, so the worst case is unclassified tasks, not wrong ones.

No HTTP calls here; Jev is called by @swamp/typesafe-ai. Each batch's answers are checked against AnswerSchema (choice, confidence 0..1) when classify parses its arguments, and answers for unknown ids are ignored.
Only Deno.stat, lstat, readDir and readTextFile, which hold no handles open. No temporary files.

README uses /path/to/your/vault and says the text, note path and heading of each task that is not withheld are sent to Jev. Tests use made-up tasks and someone@example.com. No hostnames, IPs or personal paths in shipped files.

All schemas are plain z.object except AnswerSchema, a looseObject on purpose: typesafe-ai answers carry extra fields such as probabilities, and only choice and confidence are read. heading is optional and non-empty.
result: infinite, keep 20. classified: infinite, keep 20.
Not a CRUD lifecycle behavior; it reads a vault and classifies its tasks.
run checks folder containment and existence before reading. Nothing is written outside swamp data and there is no remote state.
run writes result/result and classify writes classified/classified; each method writes one instance.
No method reads stored state; the workflow passes run's outputs and each batch's answers to classify as inputs.

model.version moves from 2026.10.23.2 (published in 2026.10.27.1) to 2026.10.23.4, with an upgrade entry: the only new setting, batchSize, has a default, so existing settings carry over unchanged (tested). The result resource's shape changes (questions becomes guidance and batches), but no method reads an old result back.
